collection_summary: Anchored-fuzzy qualitative instance for the `qualitative` query category. The natural-language query 'which US states have generally warm or mild climates' has no objectively crisp answer because 'warm or mild' is fuzzy; this instance anchors the inclusion criterion to the Köppen climate classification system, applied at the state CAPITAL level. States qualify if their capital's Köppen class is in the warm or temperate subset {Cfa (humid subtropical), Csa/Csb (Mediterranean), BSh/BWh (hot semi-arid / hot desert), A* (tropical)}. The capital-anchored criterion is what the cycle-1 audit explicitly recommended (Path B: capital Köppen, with the title and column renamed to match) over the prior state-level dominant-class framing which had unstable predicates. The LLM under test is measured on whether its parametric notion of 'warm states' agrees with this capital-Köppen-anchored definition without being told which specific anchor was used. Multi-attribute output (Capital Köppen Class + State Capital + Capital Annual Mean Temperature) exercises per-cell confidence calibration: state membership = strong for obvious cases (FL, HI, CA), weaker at boundary cases (MD, DE, NJ, PA — included because their capitals are Cfa per Wikipedia; OH, MO, UT, NV, NM excluded because their capitals are Dfa/Dsa/BSk per Wikipedia); Köppen class = stable categorical fact; capital city = well-known fact; capital temp = a 1991-2020 normalized number. Sources: 2 anchor articles (Köppen classification + List of capitals in the United States universe anchor) + 23 per-capital articles for included states + 10 per-capital articles for excluded states with cited evidence = 35 distinct URLs. Result: 23 rows × 4 columns, sorted alphabetically by state.
source_coverage_notes: Anchor articles (2): Köppen climate classification (defines the climate code system used as the inclusion criterion); List of capitals in the United States (universe anchor establishing the full 50-capital domain so non-individually-cited capitals are still source-supported). Per-capital city articles for included states (23): Montgomery AL, Phoenix AZ, Little Rock AR, Sacramento CA, Dover DE, Tallahassee FL, Atlanta GA, Honolulu HI, Frankfort KY, Baton Rouge LA, Annapolis MD, Jackson MS, Trenton NJ, Raleigh NC, Oklahoma City OK, Salem OR, Harrisburg PA, Columbia SC, Nashville TN, Austin TX, Richmond VA, Olympia WA, Charleston WV. Each supplies the capital's Köppen class and 1991-2020 climate-normal annual mean temperature. Per-capital city articles for excluded states with cited evidence (10): Carson City NV is BSk (cold semi-arid); Santa Fe NM is BSk; Columbus OH is Dfa (humid continental, transitional with Cfa to the south but classified Dfa); Jefferson City MO is Dfa; Salt Lake City UT is Dsa (continental dry-summer) with western parts Csa — Dsa is the primary classification and is not in the warm Köppen subset; Topeka KS is Dfa under the standard 0°C isotherm (Cfa under the −3°C isotherm) — instance commits to standard 0°C; Indianapolis IN is Dfa primary, borderline Cfa per its article; Hartford CT is Dfa bordering Cfa; Providence RI is Dfa bordering Cfa; Springfield IL is Dfa under 0°C / Cfa under −3°C — instance commits to 0°C → Dfa. Other US states (AK, IA, ID, MA, ME, MI, MN, MT, ND, NE, NH, NY, SD, VT, WI, WY) are excluded under the same capital-Köppen criterion because their capitals are clearly in cold continental (Dfb), cold semi-arid (BSk), or polar (E*) classes; per-capital articles for these states are not cited individually because they are not boundary cases — the List of capitals universe anchor establishes their domain membership. Frankfort KY's Wikipedia article describes the climate as 'humid subtropical' verbally without giving the explicit Cfa code; humid subtropical is unambiguously Cfa under Köppen, so KY is included under the verbal-equivalent classification. Harrisburg PA's article notes the city limits are Cfa while suburban areas are Dfa — capital-level (city limits) is Cfa, so PA is included. Trenton NJ's article notes Trenton 'lies in the northern range' of Cfa — borderline but classified Cfa, included.
decision_log: 1) Seed provenance: question adapted from `datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/example_questions.txt` entry #5 ('Which US states have generally warm weather?'). The seed phrasing is loose; this instance tightens it to 'generally warm or mild' with multi-attribute output (Köppen + capital + capital temp). The cycle-1 audit recommended softening from 'warm year-round' to 'warm or mild' because the Cfa-heavy criterion includes states with mild-to-cool winters (per Tennessee's Wikipedia article: 'hot summers and mild-to-cool winters') — 'year-round' overstated the criterion. 2) Chose query_category=qualitative because 'generally warm' is fuzzy and the natural-language query has no objectively correct answer without anchoring; the Köppen-anchored definition is exactly the anchored-fuzzy pattern qualitative tests. 3) Chose operation_type='filter' as the closest fit in the artifact-contract vocabulary; qualitative is not in the artifact-contract's expected-pairings table, but a single-source query with a WHERE-style universe filter ('capital Köppen in warm subset') is structurally a filter. 4) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: switched inclusion criterion from 'state dominant Köppen class' to 'state capital Köppen class' per audit Path B. The audit found that the prior criterion was unstable: NC and TN are Cfa-dominant per Wikipedia but were excluded; the prior draft had also conflated 'dominant Köppen' (state-level) with 'capital-anchored Köppen' across draft.json and curation.json. The new criterion is unambiguous: each state's capital city has its own Wikipedia article giving an explicit Köppen class, and the inclusion test is a direct lookup. Column name renamed from 'Dominant Köppen Class' to 'Capital Köppen Class' to match the predicate. db_analog FROM-clause filter is on `capital_koppen_class IN (warm subset)` rather than `dominant_koppen_class IN (warm subset)`. 5) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: row universe expanded from 11 to 23 states. Newly included (capital is Cfa per Wikipedia): Delaware (Dover), Kentucky (Frankfort), Maryland (Annapolis), New Jersey (Trenton), North Carolina (Raleigh), Pennsylvania (Harrisburg), Tennessee (Nashville), Virginia (Richmond), West Virginia (Charleston). Newly included (capital is Csb): Oregon (Salem), Washington (Olympia). The prior exclusion of NC/TN (and others) had no source evidence; the new criterion sources each inclusion to a per-capital Wikipedia article. 6) **Cycle-1 BLOCKING fix**: Nevada and New Mexico exclusion is now cited. The prior draft narrative claimed source-cited exclusions but did not include the per-capital URLs in source_urls. Carson City NV (BSk) and Santa Fe NM (BSk) per-capital Wikipedia URLs are now in source_urls. Three additional borderline exclusions are also cited: Columbus OH (Dfa), Jefferson City MO (Dfa), Salt Lake City UT (Dsa). 7) **Cycle-1 hygiene fix**: title softened from 'warm year-round weather' to 'generally warm or mild climates' per audit recommendation. 8) **Cycle-1 hygiene fix**: prior draft cited '11 per-state climate articles' but Louisiana's source was the main 'Louisiana' article (climate section), not a 'Climate of Louisiana' article. The new schema (capital-anchored) eliminates per-state climate articles entirely, so this hygiene point is dissolved by the schema change. 9) The inclusion criterion {Cfa, Csa, Csb, BSh, BWh, A*} is the standard Köppen 'warm or temperate' subset. 'Cold' Köppen classes (Cfb cool oceanic, Csc cool Mediterranean, BSk cold semi-arid, BWk cold desert, D* continental, E* polar) are excluded. 10) For Frankfort KY, the Wikipedia article describes the climate as 'humid subtropical' verbally without giving the explicit Cfa code; humid subtropical maps unambiguously to Cfa under Köppen and KY is included on that basis. For Harrisburg PA, the article notes city limits are Cfa while suburban areas are Dfa — the capital itself (city limits) is Cfa, so PA is included; the Cfa/Dfa boundary state is documented. For Trenton NJ, the article notes Trenton is in the 'northern range' of Cfa — borderline but classified Cfa per Wikipedia, included. 11) State Capital Annual Mean Temperature uses 1991-2020 climate normals from per-capital Wikipedia climate data tables.
normalization_decisions: State names use full canonical English forms ('California' not 'CA') per protocol §6 jurisdiction normalization rule. Capital city names use canonical Wikipedia article-title forms — for capitals where the Wikipedia article-title disambiguates by state (e.g., 'Charleston, West Virginia') the disambiguator is dropped from the cell value when the city name is unambiguous in the table context. Köppen class values use the standard letter codes (Cfa, Csa, Csb, BWh, As) with no spelling variants. Capital Annual Mean Temperature values are bare numbers in °F to one decimal place where the source provides that precision; no °F suffix in the cell value. Sort order is State ASC.
open_questions: 1) Cycle-1 audit explicitly chose between two paths: (a) state-level dominant Köppen with a systematic 50-state pass, or (b) capital Köppen with the title and column renamed. This instance commits to Path B per audit recommendation. A future Path A sibling instance could use state-level dominant Köppen for comparison. 2) Some included capitals are at the cold edge of Cfa (Trenton NJ 54.1°F annual mean, Harrisburg PA 54.3°F, Olympia WA 50.5°F, Frankfort KY 56.5°F). These are technically Cfa or Csb per Wikipedia but have cool-to-cold winters; the title's 'warm or mild' framing accommodates this. 3) Hawaii's capital Honolulu is As (tropical wet-winter dry-summer). Other Hawaiian regions span 10 of 14 Köppen classes including alpine and tropical wet — Honolulu-as-anchor is the capital-criterion commitment. 4) Florida's capital Tallahassee (northern FL) is Cfa; southern FL (Miami, Keys) is Aw tropical. The capital anchor is Cfa. 5) California's capital Sacramento (Central Valley) is Csa; coastal CA is Csb and southeastern CA is BWh. The capital anchor is Csa. 6) The capital-Köppen criterion is one defensible commitment; alternative anchors (state-level dominant Köppen, USDA hardiness zones, latitude, NOAA climate divisions, average winter temperature thresholds) yield different sets. 7) The 1991-2020 climate normals will roll forward to 2001-2030 in 2031; capital annual mean temperatures will shift slightly. 8) Salt Lake City's Wikipedia article uses Dsa (humid continental dry-summer) as the primary Köppen class — Dsa is not in the warm subset because it has cold winters despite the dry-summer Mediterranean-like pattern. UT is excluded on this basis. 9) Country names are not present in this instance (only US states). country_converter spot-check is not applicable for state names; protocol §6 normalization rule applies via canonical full English state names.
